final_answer:
Let \(k=\mathbb F_p\). Put
\[
a=T_1-I,\qquad b=T_2-I,\qquad c=T_3-I .
\]
Since \(n=p^r\), we have
\[
(1+a)^n-1=a^n,\quad (1+b)^n-1=b^n,\quad (1+c)^n-1=c^n,
\]
so the shift module is
\[
k[a,b,c]/(a^n,b^n,c^n).
\]

Let
\[
s=a+b+c.
\]
The equation \((T_1+T_2+T_3-3I)f=0\) is \(sf=0\). Because \(p\nmid 1\) and the linear change \((a,b,c)\mapsto(s,b,c)\) is invertible,
\[
k[a,b,c]/(a^n,b^n,c^n)\cong k[s,b,c]/(s^n,b^n,c^n).
\]
Thus
\[
\ker s=s^{n-1}k[b,c]/(b^n,c^n).
\]
So write
\[
f=s^{n-1}g(b,c).
\]
On this kernel, multiplication by any polynomial in \(a,b,c\) is obtained by setting
\[
a=-b-c,
\]
because any positive power of \(s\) beyond \(s^{n-1}\) vanishes.

Now \(q=n/p\) is a power of \(p\), so
\[
T_i^q=(1+a_i)^q=1+a_i^q.
\]
Set
\[
h=b^2+bc+c^2,\qquad M=bc(b+c),
\]
\[
L=(-2b-c)(b-c)(b+2c).
\]
Substituting \(a=-b-c\), the three extra conditions become
\[
h^{3q-1}g=0,\qquad M^qg=0,\qquad L^qg=0.
\]
Hence the allowed \(g\)'s form the annihilator of
\[
I=(h^{3q-1},M^q,L^q)
\]
inside \(k[b,c]/(b^n,c^n)\).

Since \(p\ge 29\), the linear factors of \(M\) and \(L\) are distinct, so \(M^q,L^q\) form a homogeneous complete intersection of degrees \(3q,3q\). Its quotient has length
\[
(3q)(3q)=9q^2
\]
and socle degree
\[
3q+3q-2=6q-2.
\]
Also
\[
\deg h^{3q-1}=2(3q-1)=6q-2,
\]
so \(h^{3q-1}\) kills exactly one top-degree socle direction. Therefore
\[
\dim k[b,c]/(M^q,L^q,h^{3q-1})=9q^2-1.
\]

By Frobenius duality for the Artinian complete intersection, the annihilator space has the same dimension:
\[
9q^2-1.
\]

It remains to impose cyclic symmetry. The cyclic map \((x,y,z)\mapsto(y,z,x)\) sends
\[
(b,c)\mapsto(c,-b-c).
\]
This order-\(3\) map fixes \(h,M,L\). On
\[
Q_0=k[b,c]/(M^q,L^q),
\]
the equivariant Hilbert trace at the nontrivial cyclic element is
\[
\frac{(1-t^{3q})^2}{(1-\omega t)(1-\omega^2 t)}\Bigg|_{t=1}=0,
\]
because \(M^q,L^q\) are invariant forms of degree \(3q\), and \(\omega,\omega^2\) are the nontrivial cube roots of unity. Passing from \(Q_0\) to
\[
Q=Q_0/(h^{3q-1})
\]
removes one invariant top-degree line, so the trace becomes \(-1\) for each nontrivial cyclic element.

Thus the fixed subspace dimension is
\[
\frac{1}{3}\bigl((9q^2-1)-1-1\bigr)=3q^2-1.
\]
Since \(q=n/p\), the answer is
\[
\boxed{3\left(\frac np\right)^2-1}.
\]
